sections.html:
Lenexa sits on the west side of the Kansas City area, in Johnson County, and covers 34.45 square miles. The 2020 census counted 57,434 residents, and a 2023 estimate puts the figure at 58,536.

The city has no school district of its own. A street address decides whether a family attends Shawnee Mission, Olathe or De Soto schools, and a buyer relocating to the area will ask early. Johnson County Transit provides local bus service, and the nearest intercity train and bus stations are in Kansas City, Missouri. A Johnson County Library branch is at Lenexa City Center, and St. James Academy, the city's first private high school, opened in 2005.

Octave Chanute, a railroad civil engineer, platted Lenexa in 1869 on land that included 10.5 acres bought from C. A. Bradshaw along a railroad right-of-way. The name comes from Na-Nex-Se, the wife of Shawnee Chief Black Hoof. In 1857 James Butler Hickok, later known as Wild Bill Hickok, staked a 160-acre claim at what is now 83rd Street and Clare Road.

The town stayed tiny for most of a century and then exploded: 2,497 people in 1960, 5,242 in 1970, 18,639 in 1980 and 34,034 in 1990. The count reached 40,238 in 2000, 48,190 in 2010 and 57,434 in 2020. The steepest jump came in the 1970s, so a large share of the housing probably dates from then on. Many houses are now 30 to 50 years old, the age when roofs, HVAC systems, water heaters and windows need replacing.

That age estimate comes from census dates and may not fit any one house, so check the year built for yours. If the major systems are original, a conventional buyer's inspector will find out, and the repair list that follows is often where a listed sale stalls.

Lenexa's job base leans toward logistics, laboratories and engineering. Garmin was born here, Kiewit Construction has its regional headquarters here, and a National Archives records center, known informally as the Caves, stores federal records from agencies in Iowa, Kansas, Missouri and Nebraska. Large employers include United Parcel Service, Quest Diagnostics/Lab One, Kiewit Power Engineers, the JC Penney Logistics Center and Alliance Data Systems.

Jobs like these keep both owner-occupied houses and rentals in demand, which is why the city runs a rental license program.

Lenexa requires a rental license before tenants or guests live in a residential rental property, and the rule covers short-term rentals. The license period runs January 1 to December 31, and the city mails printed renewal invoices in mid-November.

  • Plan to apply at least 30 business days before renting.
  • Fees start at $75 per property and depend on the type and number of properties you own in Lenexa.
  • The city inspects the exterior of every residential rental every other year, or more often if warranted.
  • An owner who lives out of state, or an out-of-state entity with no in-state manager, must name an owner's agent who lives in Johnson County, Kansas.
  • A short-term rental is a stay of less than 30 days, may not host parties or events for non-guests, and may be occupied by one person, a related group, or up to four unrelated adults.

If you own a rental you want to sell, check the license status and any open exterior violations first. The city handles status questions at permits@lenexa.com or 913-477-7725. A buyer who purchases as is can take the house with those items open, which a lender-financed buyer usually will not.

Johnson County bills Lenexa real estate tax, with first-half notices going out in mid-November. Pay the first half or the full year on or before December 20. The County Clerk figures mill levies for each taxing authority.

DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date
On or before March 1Appraised value notices mailed
March 31Appeal deadline, 30 days after mailing
November 15Bills mailed
December 20First half or full payment, and first half payment under protest

Residential owners also get a credit against the 20-mill school general levy, with 8,625 of assessed value exempt for tax years 2024 and 2025, worth $172.50. Mail payments go to a St. Louis lockbox address, and the county warns against mailing cash. Late payments accrue interest, and a missing statement does not remove it.

sections.h2: How a Lenexa deed is recorded
sections.html:
The Johnson County Register of Deeds, at 111 S. Cherry Street, Suite 1200, in Olathe, records Lenexa deeds. Walk-in hours are Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Recording costs $21.00 for page one and $17.00 for each added page. The office turns away email and fax, and sends back any document that misses margin or legibility requirements. The deed comes from the title company at closing; neither the county nor the lender holds it. For an inherited house, a Transfer on Death deed must be signed, notarized and recorded before it works as a beneficiary designation.

sections.h2: What should I compare when choosing how to sell?
sections.html:
Three things separate the routes: what you net, how long it takes and how much work you do. Each option gives up one to gain another.

  • Listing: the most exposure, paid for with showings, an appraisal and a lender's timetable.
  • Private sale: no agent fee, though disclosures and the contract fall to you.
  • Cash sale: an as-is purchase on a schedule you set, often chosen for rentals with license issues, inherited houses or houses needing a new roof or systems.

Lenexa houses are ones we buy as is. Ask for an offer and weigh it against a listing, with no obligation to accept.

Ahead of closing, collect the rental license record if the house has been rented, any city notices about the exterior and paperwork on recent roof or system work. Keep a copy of the renewal invoice too, since the city mails them in mid-November. The title company orders the search, prepares the deed and settles any unpaid tax from your proceeds. You set the closing date, so a later date is possible if you need time to move.

With tenants in the house, read the lease and tell us the move-out terms before you accept, so the offer and the closing date reflect them. A buyer who knows about a tenant up front is far less likely to ask for changes later, and a clear lease summary also helps the title company confirm who is entitled to the deposit.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license in Lenexa?
faqs.a: Yes, before any tenant or guest lives in the house, including short-term rentals. Fees start at $75 per property, the license runs January 1 to December 31, and the city inspects the exterior every other year.

faqs.q: When are Johnson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half or full amount is due on or before December 20. Tax bills are mailed around November 15, and valuation notices go out on or before March 1.

faqs.q: Which school district is Lenexa in?
faqs.a: Lenexa has no district of its own. Students attend Shawnee Mission, Olathe or De Soto district schools, depending on the address.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Lenexa property?
faqs.a: At the Johnson County Register of Deeds, 111 S. Cherry Street, Suite 1200, Olathe. The fee is $21 for the first page and $17 for each additional page.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lenexa house with an expired rental license?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as is, so an expired license or open exterior violation does not have to be resolved before closing. Contact permits@lenexa.com or 913-477-7725 to learn the license status.
